Compare the mapped drive with the known approved network path under the same account. If the path works but the mapped drive fails, check the organization's standard mapping policy.

If the path cannot be reached, verify corporate connectivity and name resolution on the approved network. If the share opens but an operation is denied, have the owner review effective folder and share rights for that operation.
Use approved instructions to reconnect the mapping when the path is reachable and no active work depends on it. Route entitlements through the data owner and preserve unsaved or offline changes.

Open the expected folder and confirm the approved operation. Use only a designated test folder for writes. Escalate multi-user path failures to Storage or Network Operations and unresolved permissions to the share owner.

handoff: Record the approved share reference, mapped versus direct-path result, network or VPN state, effective permission or error, affected scope, and validation.

title: Deleted, overwritten, or missing files
summary: Find the latest recoverable copy while preserving existing work and the evidence of what changed.

checks.text: Identify the file, original location, owner, last known good time and zone, and whether deletion, movement, overwrite, or an unsaved edit is suspected.
Check the approved workspace search, recent items, trash or recycle bin, version history, and relevant activity logs as permitted. Compare local and web views for a synced location.

Preserve any current or local-only copies and confirm the target version with the owner. For many unexpected changes, possible ransomware, or suspicious activity, route immediately to Security and preserve evidence.

Use an authorized restore method and prefer a separate recovery location when supported so existing work stays available. Have the storage or backup owner check recoverability if self-service options are absent.

Have the owner open the recovered item and verify the expected content, version time, and permissions before replacing any working copy. Escalate unavailable recovery points, broad data loss, or business-critical restores.

handoff: Record the authorized item reference, last known good time and zone, checked recovery locations, candidate version, protected existing copies, and owner validation.

title: Browser and web application errors
summary: Isolate a web workflow failure to the browser, session, managed policy, or application service.

checks.text: Capture the approved site, affected workflow, last known working time, browser version, and exact symptom. Find out whether the user can open the home page and where the workflow stops.
Compare with a second supported managed browser or profile and an authorized peer if available. Check service status and whether the failure affects another approved workflow.

If the problem follows one browser profile, check visible site settings, extension or policy status, and whether the session needs renewal. Keep authentication cookies, tokens, request bodies, and unredacted browser traces out of tickets.

Save drafts and confirm whether a transaction completed before retrying. When the app owner permits, clear only the affected site's data after explaining it may sign the user out or remove local drafts.

Repeat a safe version of the original workflow and confirm its intended result. Route unsupported or policy-managed browser settings to Endpoint Support and repeated workflow failures or server errors to the application owner.

handoff: Record the app, workflow step, browser and OS version, device and peer comparison, visible error or correlation ID, and whether any transaction may already have completed.

title: Cloud service degradation and outage
summary: Correlate a SaaS failure with tenant, region, feature, and provider incident status before assigning ownership.

checks.text: Record the failing service and workflow, start time and zone, affected users or business functions, locations or tenants, and whether a workaround exists.
Confirm with a second authorized user or service monitor on an independent path if available. Check whether other services on the same identity provider, network, or tenant also fail.
Compare the symptom with internal incident records, approved provider status, and recent changes. Check the reported region, feature, and timeline before linking tickets to an existing incident.

If the provider owns the failing dependency, have the service owner link the tenant or vendor incident and provide a sanitized problem statement with region, time, feature, and affected cohort. Track the vendor update time under the internal ticket.

After recovery, verify the original workflow with representative affected users, locations, or accounts and check for processing backlog. Escalate sustained business-critical impact, uncertain scope, or an expanding outage to the incident lead.

handoff: Record impact and current trend, start time and zone, independent checks, correlated incident or change, approved workaround, current owner, and next update time.

title: Application licensing and activation
summary: Distinguish missing entitlements, exhausted seats, and device or account activation problems.

checks.text: Capture the product, edition, device, account context, activation stage, and error. Check whether this is a new install, replacement device, renewal, or a previously working installation.
Ask an authorized license operator to confirm the correct product and tenant, active assignment, provisioning state, and available seats where applicable.
Check whether the same approved account can use the web version or another permitted device. For managed license servers, ask the owner to confirm service status and approved connectivity.
Use the approved sign-in and activation workflow after confirming entitlement. Route new allocation, seat transfers, expired subscriptions, or out-of-policy editions to Software Asset Management.
Confirm the app reports the correct activation state and the entitled feature works. Escalate recurring activation failures with the exact error and time. Keep product keys out of tickets and chat.

handoff: Record product, edition and version, activation error and timestamp, license assignment or seat status, affected scope, and validation or provisioning request reference.

title: Application roles and provisioning
summary: Distinguish successful sign-in from missing app access, assignment, role, or workspace membership.
keywords: don't have access to the app
don't have access to an application

checks.text: Identify the app and tenant, the authorized operation expected, the actual error, and the last known working time. Separate sign-in failure from missing permission after a successful sign-in.
Confirm the user is in the correct account, tenant, workspace, and environment. Determine whether the entire app is missing or only an action, dataset, or resource is unavailable.

Ask the authorized app owner to check approved assignment, group membership, license, app role, and provisioning status as applicable. Compare expected access with documented roles while protecting other users' data.

Use the normal access request or approved correction process for the minimum required role. Confirm the effective assignment with the owner before refreshing the app session through the normal sign-in workflow.

Have the user verify the originally requested operation within their approved scope. Route wrong role or resource access to the application owner, provisioning errors to Identity, and unexplained elevated access to Security.

handoff: Record app and tenant, authorized role and operation, sign-in outcome, provisioning status or error, access request or owner reference, and final operation check.

title: IT service requests and fulfillment
summary: Route onboarding, software, equipment, and routine changes through the correct fulfillment workflow.

checks.text: Confirm the requested service, business need, due date and time zone, and which person or asset is in scope. If something previously worked and now fails, record an incident for the affected service.
Select the current service catalog item and check its required approvals and prerequisites. Link related requests so device, software, and account tasks can proceed in the right order.
Use the normal approver and data owner workflow for access or procurement. Route urgent offboarding, unusual entitlement requests, or conflicting dates to the responsible owner.
Record the fulfillment owner, the next dependency, and the update due date. Use approved deployment and handover channels, and confirm responsibility for any asset return or access removal.

Verify required assets or services reach the intended recipient and work within the approved scope. For offboarding, have the authorized owner confirm completed actions against the request before closing.

handoff: Record request reference, authorized scope, due date and zone, approval status, dependencies, fulfillment owner, and acceptance or closure criteria.
